title: Smother a pan fire with a fire blanket and leave it in place
instruction: Put out the pan fire with the fire blanket.
context: Fire-blanket makers' instructions and fire-service advice agree: hold the blanket by its tapes, hands shielded behind it, lay it over the pan (never throw it), cover the pan fully, as a gap at the rim lets air in and the fire flares back, and leave it on until the pan is cool. The instruction gives only the goal. This is not a plain cloth-cover task (as in deformable-object benchmarks): a limp sheet lowered in place piles up in a strip, so both top corners must be carried across the pan while lowering until it seals all four rim edges, and the unstated fire rules (no throwing, hands out of the flames, no lifting to check) are scored. Unlike #1104 (a stiff dressing set flat on a wound, touched only at its edges), the sheet is limp and draping it over a raised rim is the test; unlike #1130 (a hinged laminate settles on a drawer front as its supports are pulled), the robot lays it; unlike #1016 (aim an extinguisher's spray), nothing is aimed. Done by: cooks (O*NET 35-2014.00, 35-2012.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the table, everything square to the table. Hob: a fixed black glass-ceramic plate 24 x 30 cm, 0.6 cm thick, centred at x 33.5, y 0. Pan: a fixed carbon-steel frying pan 12 x 12 cm outside, 1 cm walls standing 4.5 cm on the hob (rim at +5.1), centred at x 32, y 0; opening 10 x 10 cm. Inside: cooking oil 2 cm below the rim, alight (five fixed 2 x 2 x 1.5 cm orange flame blocks standing on it, tops 5 mm below the rim). Fire blanket: woven glass-fibre fabric, 24 cm wide (y) and 28 cm long, made of seven 4 cm bands (10 g each; the top hem 14 g) that bend freely along its length; two black polyester tapes (1.6 x 2.5 x 3.5 cm) stand up from its top edge at y +9.5 and -9.5, and a steel hang pin sticks out at each end of the top hem. It hangs by the pins from two upward-open steel U-hooks on posts at x 19, y +-13.6, its top edge at +12.3: the top three bands hang down at x 19 and the lower four lie flat on the worktop toward the robot (x 3 to 19).
scoring: From the blanket bands' poses and the grippers' tool points (on a real rig: top-down video). An opening point (25, a 5 x 5 grid over the opening) is covered when a band lies over it at a height from 1 cm below the flame tops to 4 cm above the rim; a rim point (16, four along each rim edge) is sealed when a band lies over it within 2 cm above the rim. The fire is out once all 41 points have been covered for 1 s in a row. Latched for the trial, score 0: (a) a gripper's tool point inside the zone over the opening grown by 2 cm, up to 8 cm above the rim; (b) thrown or dropped: a band whose lowest point is more than 4 cm above the rim falls faster than 0.3 m/s while no tool point is within 4 cm of either tape; (c) after the fire is out, an opening point uncovered for 0.5 s in a row (lifted to check). Otherwise: 1.0 when the fire is out, all 41 points are still covered, no tool point is within 2.5 cm of any band and every band is still (moved under 0.3 mm and turned under 0.5 deg since the last step); success when that holds 1 s. 0.75 when the fire is out; 0.5 when all 25 opening points are covered; 0.25 when the blanket is off its hooks and covers some opening point; 0 otherwise. Scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Hang the blanket back on its two hooks by its pins with its lower four bands laid flat on the worktop toward the robot; the hob, pan, oil, flame blocks and hook stand do not move.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The blanket is seven rigid 4 cm bands on PhysX hinges with 0.0008 N m Coulomb friction (mechkit.py, in this folder): it bends along its length only, so its sides lie flat on the side rims instead of draping down them. No fire model: the flames are fixed orange blocks and 'out' means the opening and the rim stay covered for 1 s. A real fire blanket is about 1 m square; this one is scaled to the 12 cm pan.
